Check what fitted facility counts identify in an allocation model

Source: R/07-allocation_check.R
check_allocation.Rd

Compares a fitted allocation with two simpler allocations on the same loss and observed targets, and summarizes the travel times the allocations imply. The check reports only: it never changes or replaces the fit.

Usage

check_allocation(model, fit, trip_breaks = c(30, 60, 120))

# S3 method for class 'ae_allocation_check'
print(x, digits = 4, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ae_allocation_check'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

model

The corrected CLM from clm_allocation() that was fitted.

fit

The ae_multistart_fit returned by fit_allocation() for model. A search with no selected fit cannot be checked.

trip_breaks

Positive travel times (in the prepared travel units) for which the share of expected trips longer than each value is reported.

x

An ae_allocation_check.

digits

Significant digits for printed values.

...

Unused.

row.names, optional

Standard as.data.frame() arguments; unused.

Value

An ae_allocation_check with a comparators table (loss, loss difference from the fit, parameters, need-weighted contact and implied trips), the exact comparator parameters (those of no_decay are the re-optimized parameters other than sigma, an empty vector when the model fits only sigma), the selected fit's parameter boundary flags, search_at_edge, logical flags, and poisson_floor (for a Poisson fit: its floor eps and the number of cells with positive observed counts modelled below it, which cap the loss; NULL otherwise). Use print() or as.data.frame().

Details

Facility counts constrain where predicted loads fall but not where users live. When facility capacity closely tracks the observed counts, an allocation that ignores travel time can reproduce the counts as well as, or better than, a distance-decay allocation. The fitted decay then depends on the travel support, such as a catchment limit on the prepared travel times, rather than on the counts. The comparators are:

  • fitted: the selected fit, recomputed at its parameters.

  • no_decay: distance decay switched off within the prepared travel support: every finite travel time gets the same weight, whatever decay kernel the model uses, and absent edges stay absent. Origins choose among reachable facilities in proportion to attractiveness, and the outside mass is re-optimized when the model fits it. Its reported parameters leave out the decay parameter sigma, which this allocation does not use.

  • capacity_only: facility loads proportional to attractiveness, ignoring travel entirely, with one fitted scale factor. Available for facility utilization targets only.

When the model fits the attractiveness exponent beta, it is re-optimized in both comparators. Comparator searches start from the fit's own scale and widen while the optimum lies at the search edge; flags records any search that still ends at an edge.

Implied trips are one-way travel times weighted by expected flows, using the prepared travel times. Flows on absent edges (possible only for capacity_only) have no travel time: the quantiles and the shares of trips longer than each break are among flows on reachable edges, and the absent share is reported separately. To see how the fit depends on a catchment limit, prepare the inputs again with travel beyond the limit set to Inf, refit, and check each fit.
